Team / Alex,

We have the private deployment cutover for ACME scheduled Tue 9/18 02:00-04:00 PT. Before we go green, I want to confirm two things in this thread: (1) the blackout contingency we will use if the fabric shows instability during the first 30 minutes, and (2) the first-hour playbook items that the on-call and SRE teams will execute in sequence.

Attached are a lean first-hour playbook and the latest annotated network diagram. Key asks:
- Irene: can you confirm the three-step blackout path (traffic drain -> region fallback -> customer throttled mode) is scripted and tested in staging?
- Vivek: provide the KV cache warmup hook and expected warmup duration for the primary model fleet (attach script).
- Karthik / Monica: who owns the immediate procurement/sign-off if an SLA credit needs to be invoked?
- Alex / ACME ops: confirm you can tolerate a 12-minute planned pause for database migration in the second window if we request it.

I'll run a 30-minute pre-cutover runbook playback Monday EOD (09/17 16:30 PT) — invite to follow. If there's anything missing from the checklist, flag it here.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks, this is good. Quick status from SRE: 
- Blackout contingency implemented as a three-stage automated policy in staging. Sequence implemented as:
  1) Traffic drain to warm lanes (30s graceful drain)
  2) Route switch to fallback model variant in same region (policy TTL = 5 min)
  3) If errors persist, region failover to secondary capacity with throttled tokens (rate limiter at 60% baseline)
- We've exercised steps 1 & 2 against canary for both VPC and on-prem edges; step 3 is simulated only (need a dry-run in prod window).

Action items I will own before the playback:
- Add an automatic slack alert to #cutover-ops for each transition and a one-click rollback link (runbook command).
- Validate ACLs on the fallback instances (expected to be identical to primary).
- Provide a short checklist for the war room to confirm every 5 mins during first 30 minutes.

I attached the small runbook excerpt with the exact run commands. Vivek — can you confirm the expected KV warmup time for the 1M-token baseline? Also, Karthik — we'll need your sign-off path if we escalate to credits.

—Irene
Irene Choi | Director, Production Reliability | Redwood Inference

Irene / team,

Confirmed: KV warmup hook attached (kv-warmup-hook.sh). Estimated warmup: 7-10 minutes for the primary keyspace at cold start with parallelism=16 on the dedicated pool. Notes:
- Warmup should be kicked at -10m relative to traffic cutover (i.e., 01:50 PT) to get headroom.
- If we see >1.8s p95 response during warmup, abort and move to fallback-model-variant (policy in runbook).

Two automation suggestions:
1) Add a liveness probe that flips a lightweight header when cache reaches target hit rate (so downstream routers can detect readiness).
2) Wire an automatic traffic hold for 12 minutes if the DB migration flag is detected from ACME (this avoids half-live requests).

I'll update the script to emit a 'warmup:complete' event to the cutover bridge (Zoom + slack webhook) and attach logs to the Drive folder.

—Vivek
